content: He who laughs at everything is a fool; he who weeps at everything is miserable; he who observes with discernment is wise.
author: Ancient Greek Proverbs
sourceWork: Democritus and Heraclitus (The Laughing and Weeping Philosophers)
explanation: Democritus mocked all human striving as ridiculous comedy; Heraclitus wept over all human folly as tragic ruin. The true sage transcends both extremes: observing human nature with compassionate clarity, neither numbing out through cynicism nor drowning in despair.
practicalInsight: Observe a tense cultural or workplace dispute today as an impartial witness, with calm compassion rather than panic.
reflectionPrompt: Do you oscillate between cynical mockery and overwhelming despair, instead of resting in calm discernment?
